items.label: qe-fig-001
items.note: Do not set figure size unless necessary

children.value: Do not set figure size unless necessary

invalid.because: primitive names another primitive, so a consumer would dispatch on the wrong shape
primitive is missing entirely, so the node cannot be dispatched without the class string
class is missing the qe-dv-bar-list token that every consumer selects on
class repeats a base token, which the directive's normalisation never produces
tone is outside the closed vocabulary neutral|accent|good|warn|bad
an item is missing the required note key, which must be an explicit null, not absent
an item value is a string, so bar length and the printed number are not a number
an item carries a misspelt key, which additionalProperties must catch rather than ignore
total is zero, which cannot be a denominator
items is empty, so there is nothing to draw and the fallback carries a header row and no data rows
the fallback value cell carries the wrong span class, so a theme cannot style it
children hold a card node, which myst-to-tex drops silently from a LaTeX export
contract is a number rather than the version string
a data row carries a header cell, which makes myst-to-tex rule the table after every line and, on the long-table path, count every row as a header until the body loop skips them all
the fallback table has no header row, so the plain rendering leaves the reader with three unnamed columns of ids, titles and numbers
a note-less row omits its note cell, and myst-to-typst emits cells as one flat positional sequence, so every later cell shifts one column left for the rest of the table
an inner span carries contract and primitive, which only the root node may do
the root carries a top-level label, which myst-cli's embed transform deletes from every node that is not a crossReference, cite, footnote reference, caption number or link

the retired `naLabel` is carried on the root: the draft let each block spell a missing value for itself, contract 1.0 spells it one way — `null` in the properties, an em dash in the fallback — so a node still carrying the option sends a consumer looking for a string that means nothing
